text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tight security at ward of Ibadan University Teaching Hospital in southwest where leader of opposition NADECO group Michael Ajasin, 88, is being treated for undisclosed ailment.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha to meet on Thursday with all agencies implementing democratisation plan to appraise how the plan to restore civil rule by October 1998 is going.
- Five people arraigned before a tribunal in Lagos for allegedly tampering with oil products pipeline last October.
- Nigerian banks begin search for funds to meet new government requirement that they raise their minimum capital base to 500 million naira from 50 million naira.
- Military ruler Abacha calls for democratisation of U.N. Security Council with inclusion of Nigeria, Brazil and India as permanent members.
- Oil minister Dan Etete to inaugurate a committee in the capital Abuja on Thursday to monitor the oil industry and ensure compliance by oil companies with Nigerian regulations.
- State oil firm NNPC reschedules its debt to the ports authority after paying 100 million naira to resolve dispute that led to aviation fuel shortage.
